correctness.rationale: Unique projection is fixed by the stabilizer of a rank-k partial permutation, reducing n² variables to four scalar orbit entries. Row/column sums and the strict Frobenius objective show matched off-diagonal weight vanishes, leaving a one-variable quadratic uniquely minimized at cross-block weight 1/[n+q(q+1)]; all entries are feasible. The exact minimum q(q+2)/[n+q(q+1)] produces n+1 strictly ordered vertex shells. Convexity of distance squared and the unique rank-zero maximum prove unique zero-matrix Hausdorff extremizer even among nonvertices. An exact local saddle-point ratio and Stirling/tightness argument yield N(0,1/2) scaled deficiency; the smooth metric map gives N(0,1/8). The actual packaged verifier checks 33 rational cases, 46,230 permutation inequalities, and 18 independent constrained-optimization cases. Computation supports but does not prove unbounded-n results.

value.rationale: Euclidean completion of a missing-edge perfect matching is naturally the distance from the partial-assignment polytope to its Birkhoff face. The result exactly determines every nearest projection across all vertex ranks, the complete metric shells with multiplicities, the full-polytope unique deep hole, and a sharp sqrt(n) transition of completion error. The typical error 1/2 and its n^{-1/4} Gaussian fluctuations give a geometric interpretation of known deficiency statistics. These structural facts are not a routine numeric projection output, arbitrary finite table, or mere restatement of general algorithms.
